text:
This policy describes the benefits Helios Systems offers, who is eligible for
each, and when elections can be made or changed.

Eligibility for every benefit is determined by employment type as recorded in
the HR system field `employment_type`.

| Employment type | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| **Full-time** | Regular employee scheduled for 30 or more hours per week |
| **Part-time** | Regular employee scheduled for 20 – 29 hours per week |
| **Temporary** | Employee on a fixed-term contract of 6 months or less |
| **Intern** | Enrolled student in a defined internship program |
| **Contractor** | Engaged through a vendor or as an independent contractor; not a Helios employee |

Contractors are not eligible for any Helios benefit. Questions about contractor
compensation are handled by Procurement, not People Operations.

| Benefit | Full-time | Part-time | Temporary | Intern |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Medical, dental, vision | Yes | Yes (employee-only subsidy) | No | No |
| Health Savings Account (HSA) | Yes, with HDHP plan | Yes, with HDHP plan | No | No |
| 401(k) — employee deferral | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes, if age 21+ |
| 401(k) — company match | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Life and AD&D insurance | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Short-term disability | Yes | No | No | No |
| Long-term disability | Yes | No | No | No |
| Paid parental leave | Yes | Yes, pro-rated | No | No |
| PTO | Yes | Yes, pro-rated | No | No |
| Floating holidays | 2 per year | 1 per year | No | No |
| Wellness stipend | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Learning stipend | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Home-office stipend | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Commuter benefit | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Employee Assistance Program (EAP) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

| Benefit | Coverage begins |
| --- | --- |
| Medical, dental, vision | First day of the month following **30 days** of employment |
| Life, AD&D, disability | First day of the month following **30 days** of employment |
| 401(k) deferral | First payroll following **60 days** of employment |
| 401(k) company match | First payroll following **12 months** of employment |
| Wellness and learning stipends | Immediately on hire |
| Paid parental leave | After **12 months** of continuous service |

An employee who has not yet satisfied a waiting period is **not eligible** for
that benefit, even if they have made an election.

Helios offers three medical plans:

| Plan | Type | Employee premium (monthly) | Deductible (individual) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Helios Core | PPO | $95 | $1,500 |
| Helios Plus | PPO | $180 | $750 |
| Helios Saver | HDHP with HSA | $40 | $3,200 |

Helios contributes **$1,000 per year** to the HSA of employees enrolled in the
Helios Saver plan, deposited in equal amounts each pay period.

Dependent coverage is available for a spouse, domestic partner, and children up
to age 26. Dependent verification documentation must be provided within **30
days** of adding a dependent, or coverage for that dependent is cancelled.

- Helios matches **100% of the first 3%** of eligible pay deferred, plus
  **50% of the next 2%**, for a maximum match of 4% of eligible pay.
- The match is subject to the 12-month service requirement in Section 4.
- Employer match vests on a **two-year cliff**: an employee who separates before
  completing 24 months of service forfeits the entire unvested match. Employee
  deferrals are always 100% vested.
- Contribution changes may be made at any time and take effect the following
  pay period.

heading_path: 7. Open Enrollment and Qualifying Life Events
text:
Annual open enrollment runs **November 1 – November 20** each year, with
elections effective January 1. Employees who do not actively elect are enrolled
in the same medical plan as the prior year, except that **HSA and FSA
contributions reset to zero** and must be re-elected every year.

heading_path: 7. Open Enrollment and Qualifying Life Events

text:
| Stipend | Amount | Frequency | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wellness | $75 | Monthly | Gym, fitness apps, therapy, nutrition |
| Learning and development | $2,000 | Annual | Courses, certifications, conferences, books |
| Home office | $750 | One-time on hire | Furniture and ergonomics; see `POL-EQUIP-001` |
| Home office refresh | $300 | Every 3 years | Remote and hybrid employees only |
| Internet | $60 | Monthly | Remote employees only; hybrid employees not eligible |

Stipends are reimbursed through the expense system under `POL-EXP-001` and are
taxable where required by law. Unused stipend amounts do not carry over.

A change in employment type that affects eligibility is a qualifying life event.
Benefits change on the effective date of the employment-type change, not the
date of the request. An employee moving from full-time to part-time loses
short-term and long-term disability coverage and moves to the employee-only
medical subsidy.

Medical, dental, and vision coverage ends on the **last day of the month** in
which employment ends. COBRA continuation election materials are sent within 14
days of separation. See `POL-PTO-001` Section 8 for PTO payout at separation.

doc_title: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
heading_path: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
text:
Helios Systems is committed to a workplace free from harassment, discrimination,
retaliation, and violence. This policy applies to all workers, in every location,
and to all work-related settings including offices, remote work, business travel,
company events, and work-related digital channels.

doc_title: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
heading_path: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy

doc_title: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
heading_path: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
text:
Adverse treatment based on a protected characteristic — including race, colour,
national origin, ancestry, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender
identity or expression, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status,
marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law — is
prohibited in every employment decision.

doc_title: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
heading_path: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
text:
Unwelcome conduct based on a protected characteristic that creates an
intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment, or that is made a
condition of employment. This includes, without limitation: slurs, derogatory
jokes, mockery, display of offensive images, and repeated unwanted contact.

doc_title: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
heading_path: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
text:
Unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favours, and other verbal,
visual, or physical conduct of a sexual nature. This includes *quid pro quo*
harassment, where a term of employment is conditioned on submission to such
conduct, and hostile-environment harassment.

3.4 Bullying and Abusive Conduct
Repeated conduct a reasonable person would find hostile or intimidating,
including verbal abuse, deliberate humiliation, sabotage of a colleague's work,
and exclusion intended to harm.

doc_title: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
heading_path: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
text:
Any adverse action against a person because they reported a concern in good
faith, participated in an investigation, or refused to participate in prohibited
conduct. **Retaliation is prohibited even where the original report is not
substantiated.** Retaliation is treated as seriously as the underlying conduct.

3.6 Workplace Violence
Threats, intimidation, physical aggression, and possession of weapons on Helios
premises are prohibited. Threats of imminent harm are an emergency: contact
local emergency services first, then Helios Security at +1-555-0100.

doc_title: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
heading_path: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
text:
A worker may report a concern through any of the following. There is no
requirement to report to a direct manager, and no requirement to raise the issue
with the other person first.

| Channel | Contact | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct manager | — | Manager must escalate to HR within 24 hours |
| Skip-level manager | — | Where the concern involves the direct manager |
| HR Business Partner | Named in the HR system | |
| People Operations | `people-ops@helios.example.com` | |
| Ethics Hotline | 1-555-0199 or `ethics.helios.example.com` | **Anonymous**, 24/7, operated by an independent third party |
| Legal | `legal@helios.example.com` | For legal or regulatory concerns |

Reports involving an executive officer are routed directly to the General
Counsel and the Audit Committee of the Board.

doc_title: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
heading_path: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
text:
A manager who receives a report of harassment, discrimination, retaliation, or
violence — or who observes such conduct — **must** escalate it to People
Operations or Legal within **24 hours**. Managers may not:

- investigate a harassment or discrimination allegation themselves;
- promise confidentiality beyond what this policy provides;
- discourage a worker from reporting; or
- discuss the report with anyone who does not have a need to know.

Failure to escalate is itself a violation of this policy.

doc_title: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
heading_path: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
text:
1. **Intake** — People Operations or Legal acknowledges the report within
   **2 business days**.
2. **Assessment** — a determination is made about scope, interim measures, and
   whether outside counsel or an external investigator is required. Interim
   measures may include a schedule change or reporting-line change, and must not
   disadvantage the reporting party.
3. **Investigation** — interviews with the reporting party, the responding
   party, and witnesses; review of relevant records. Investigations are
   conducted by trained investigators.
4. **Findings** — a determination is made on a preponderance-of-the-evidence
   standard.
5. **Outcome** — both parties are informed of the outcome and of any action
   affecting them. Target time from intake to outcome is **30 calendar days**;
   complex matters may take longer, and the reporting party receives a status
   update at least every 14 days.

doc_title: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
heading_path: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
text:
Reports are handled with as much confidentiality as is possible while still
conducting a thorough investigation. Information is shared strictly on a
need-to-know basis. Helios cannot promise complete anonymity where the identity
of the reporting party is necessary to investigate, but an anonymous report may
be made through the Ethics Hotline.

doc_title: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
heading_path: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
text:
Substantiated violations result in action proportionate to the conduct,
including coaching, written warning, mandatory training, reassignment, demotion,
loss of bonus or equity, or termination. Knowingly making a false report in bad
faith is itself a violation; a good-faith report that is not substantiated is
never a violation.

doc_title: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
heading_path: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
text:
Workers must disclose any situation where personal interests could conflict with
Helios's interests, including:

- a romantic relationship within a direct or indirect reporting line — this must
  be disclosed to People Operations, which will arrange a reporting-line change;
- outside employment, advisory roles, or board seats;
- a financial interest in a Helios customer, supplier, or competitor; and
- hiring or managing a family member or close personal contact.

Disclosure is made to `people-ops@helios.example.com`. Disclosure is not itself
a violation; failure to disclose is.

doc_title: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
heading_path: Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment, and Reporting Policy
text:
Workers may not offer or accept anything of value intended to improperly
influence a business decision. Gifts and hospitality with a value over **$100**
must be declined or disclosed. Facilitation payments are prohibited without
exception. Anything involving a government official requires prior Legal
approval.

11 Support Resources
The Employee Assistance Program offers free, confidential counselling 24/7 at
1-555-0177 and is independent of Helios management. Using the EAP is never
reported to a manager.

12 Contacts
People Operations: `people-ops@helios.example.com`
Legal: `legal@helios.example.com`
Ethics Hotline (anonymous, 24/7): 1-555-0199
Security Operations Center (24/7): +1-555-0100
Emergency: contact local emergency services first

This policy describes how Helios Systems issues, maintains, refreshes, and
recovers company equipment. It applies to every worker issued a Helios asset,
including contractors and interns.

All Helios equipment remains the property of Helios Systems at all times,
regardless of how long it has been in an employee's possession.

Every new worker receives a standard equipment bundle determined by their role
family. Requests outside the standard bundle require manager approval and are
reviewed by IT Operations.

  Role family            Laptop                      Additional
  ---------------------  --------------------------  ------------------------
  Engineering            16" MacBook Pro, 32GB RAM   External SSD, docking
                         or Dell XPS 15 (Linux)      station, 27" monitor
  Data / ML              16" MacBook Pro, 64GB RAM   27" monitor, GPU cloud
                                                     allocation
  Design                 16" MacBook Pro, 32GB RAM   Colour-calibrated 27"
                                                     monitor, drawing tablet
  Sales / Customer       14" MacBook Air, 16GB RAM   Headset, portable monitor
  Success
  Corporate functions    14" MacBook Air, 16GB RAM   24" monitor
  (Finance, People,
  Legal, Marketing)
  Support Engineering    14" MacBook Pro, 32GB RAM   Dual 24" monitors, headset

All workers additionally receive: a headset, a USB-C hub, a laptop stand, a
keyboard and mouse, and a hardware security key (see POL-SEC-001 Section 5).

Mobile phones are issued only to workers in on-call rotations, Field Sales, and
the executive team. Other workers may claim the monthly phone allowance of $40
instead.

Asset                 Refresh interval    Notes
  --------------------  ------------------  ------------------------------
  Laptop                36 months           Measured from asset issue date
  Monitor               60 months           Replaced on failure otherwise
  Headset               24 months
  Mobile phone          24 months
  Keyboard / mouse      On failure          No fixed interval
  Security key          On failure          Replacement requires identity
                                            verification

Refresh is automatic: IT contacts the employee approximately 30 days before the
laptop refresh date to schedule the swap. Employees may defer a refresh once,
by up to 6 months.

Early replacement outside the refresh cycle requires a documented business
justification and Director approval, except for hardware failure, which is
always replaced at no cost to the team's budget.

Remote and hybrid employees receive a one-time home-office stipend of $750 on
hire, and a refresh stipend of $300 every three years. The stipend is
administered under POL-BEN-001 Section 8 and is claimed through the expense
system.

The stipend covers desks, chairs, lighting, and ergonomic accessories. It does
not cover computing equipment, which IT purchases directly (Section 4.2).

Employees must not buy laptops, monitors, peripherals, or software personally
and submit an expense claim. Such claims are denied under POL-EXP-001
Section 8. All computing equipment is ordered by IT Operations and shipped to
the employee's registered address.
citation: POL-EQUIP-001 §4.2 Computing Equipment Is Never Self-Purchased

text:
Any employee may request a remote ergonomic assessment at no cost. Equipment
recommended by an ergonomic assessment, or required as a documented workplace
accommodation, is purchased by Helios in addition to the stipend and does not
reduce the stipend balance.

Normal wear and accidental damage are covered by Helios at no cost to the
employee. There is no deductible and no charge-back to the employee or team.

Loss or theft must be reported to IT and to the Security Operations Center
within 4 hours of discovery, per POL-SEC-001 Section 3.3. A police report is
required for theft claims.

Repeated loss - three or more devices lost within a rolling 24-month period -
is reviewed by IT Operations with the employee's manager and People Operations.

Deliberate damage or sale of Helios equipment is treated as misappropriation of
company property under POL-CONDUCT-001.

Incidental personal use of Helios equipment is permitted within the limits of
POL-SEC-001 Section 6. Employees must not:

  - allow family members or other third parties to use Helios equipment;
  - store personal media libraries or personal financial records on a Helios
    device;
  - remove MDM enrolment or the endpoint security agent; or
  - install unapproved software.

Employees should assume that anything stored on a Helios device may be reviewed
by Helios where there is a legitimate business or legal reason to do so.

Workers travelling to a location on the Elevated Risk list in POL-SEC-001
Section 8 must travel with a clean loaner laptop and loaner phone, requested
from IT with a minimum of 5 business days' notice. The primary device must not
travel to these locations.

Loaner devices are also available for any international trip on request, and are
recommended where the employee will be working from a shared or public space.

Loaner devices must be returned within 5 business days of return travel and are
wiped and re-imaged on receipt.

All Helios equipment must be returned by the employee's last day of employment.
IT sends a prepaid shipping kit to remote employees approximately 7 days before
the separation date.

  Asset                     Return required
  ------------------------  ----------------------------------------
  Laptop                    Yes
  Monitor(s)                Yes
  Mobile phone (issued)     Yes
  Security key              Yes
  Headset                   Yes
  Docking station, hub      Yes
  Keyboard, mouse           No - employee may retain
  Laptop stand              No - employee may retain
  Home office furniture     No - purchased with stipend, employee
                            retains ownership

Equipment not returned within 21 days of the separation date is invoiced to the
former employee at fair market value, and where permitted by state law, may be
deducted from final pay.

Employees must not wipe, reset, or factory-restore a device before returning it;
IT performs a forensic-safe wipe after data-retention checks.

Equipment required as a reasonable accommodation is provided by Helios at no
cost to the employee or the team budget, and is not subject to the standard
issue limits in Section 2. Accommodation requests are handled confidentially by
People Operations; IT is informed only of the equipment to be provided, never of
the underlying medical information.

Security Operations Center: +1-555-0100 (24/7)

In addition to the observed holidays above, each full-time employee receives

- Floating holidays may be used for any purpose, including religious or cultural

- Floating holidays require the same advance notice as a 1 – 2 day PTO request
  (3 business days; see `POL-PTO-001`, Section 3.1).
- Floating holidays **do not carry over** and are forfeited if unused by
  December 31.
- Floating holidays are **not paid out** at separation.

When a US holiday falls on a Saturday, it is observed on the preceding Friday.
When it falls on a Sunday, it is observed on the following Monday. The observed
date, not the calendar date, is the paid day off.

Employees observe the holiday schedule of their **assigned office location** as
recorded in the HR system, not the schedule of the location they happen to be
working from on a given day. An employee temporarily working from another
country under `POL-INTL-001` continues to observe their home-location schedule.

Employees whose work requires coverage on a holiday (for example, on-call
support) receive an alternate day off, scheduled with their manager within 60
days of the holiday.

6 Holidays During Leave

`POL-LEAVE-002` are treated according to that policy and are not separately
credited.

doc_title: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
heading_path: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
This policy defines how Helios Systems information and systems must be handled.
It applies to all workers — employees, contractors, and interns — and to all
devices used for Helios work, in any location.

doc_title: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
heading_path: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
All Helios information falls into one of four classifications. The
classification determines the handling requirements.

| Class | Definition | Examples | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Public** | Approved for external release | Marketing site, published docs | No restriction |
| **Internal** | Default for business information | Org charts, roadmaps, meeting notes | Helios accounts only |
| **Confidential** | Would harm Helios or a customer if disclosed | Customer data, contracts, source code, unreleased financials | Encrypted at rest and in transit; access on a need-to-know basis |
| **Restricted** | Legally protected or highly sensitive | Employee PII, health data, payroll, security keys, M&A material | Named-individual access only; access logged; never on personal devices |

When a classification is unclear, treat the information as **Confidential**
until Information Security advises otherwise.

doc_title: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
heading_path: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy

doc_title: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
heading_path: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
Personal devices may be used **only** for: Helios email, calendar, and the
Helios chat client, each through an approved managed application. Personal
devices must have a device passcode and current OS version enrolled in the
Helios MDM.

Personal devices may **never** be used to access Restricted data, to store
Helios source code, or to perform any work while outside the home country
(see `POL-INTL-001` Section 6).

doc_title: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
heading_path: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
Report a lost or stolen device to the Security Operations Center immediately,
and in any case within **4 hours** of discovery, at
`security@helios.example.com` or +1-555-0100. Helios will remotely wipe the
device. Late reporting is itself a policy violation.

doc_title: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
heading_path: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
Employees working outside a Helios office must:

- hold calls involving Confidential or Restricted information where they cannot
  be overheard — not in coworking common areas, cafés, aircraft, or trains;
- use a privacy screen when working on Confidential material in any public
  space;
- never leave a device unattended and unlocked; and
- shred or securely dispose of printed Confidential material.

Video calls involving Restricted data require a private room and a blurred or
virtual background.

doc_title: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
heading_path: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
- Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all Helios systems. SMS-based
  MFA is not accepted; use the Helios authenticator app or a hardware key.
- Passwords must be unique per system and generated and stored in the
  company-provided password manager.
- Sharing credentials is prohibited without exception, including with a manager
  or with IT support.
- Access is granted on a least-privilege basis and is reviewed quarterly.
- Report suspected credential compromise within **1 hour** of discovery.

doc_title: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
heading_path: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy

doc_title: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
heading_path: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
An Information Security review is required before:

- any work from outside the employee's home country, of any duration
  (`POL-INTL-001` Section 4.5);
- domestic temporary work exceeding **10 consecutive business days**
  (`POL-REMOTE-001` Section 5); and
- any travel to a country on the Elevated Risk list (Section 8).

The review is requested in the same Workday flow as the travel or remote-work
request and typically completes within **5 business days**.

doc_title: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
heading_path: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
- Connect through the Helios VPN for **all** work activity while outside the
  registered work location. Public Wi-Fi without VPN is prohibited.
- Use a company eSIM or personal hotspot in preference to hotel or café Wi-Fi.
- Enable device-location services so a lost device can be traced.
- Do not connect to Helios systems from a device you do not control, including
  hotel business-centre computers.
- Physical device custody must be maintained at borders; do not place Helios
  devices in checked baggage.

doc_title: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
heading_path: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
Travel to an Elevated Risk country requires a clean loaner laptop and loaner
phone, issued by IT with at least **5 business days'** notice. The employee's
primary device must not travel. Loaner devices are wiped on return.

doc_title: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
heading_path: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
The following locations require a loaner device, pre-travel briefing, and
post-travel device wipe: China, Russia, Belarus, Iran, North Korea, Syria, and
Cuba. Work from sanctioned jurisdictions is prohibited regardless of device.

The Elevated Risk list is maintained by Information Security and may change; the
current list is authoritative at the time of travel.

doc_title: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
heading_path: Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
Report any suspected security incident — phishing, data exposure, malware,
unauthorised access, or lost device — to `security@helios.example.com`
immediately. Helios does not penalise good-faith reports, including reports of
an employee's own mistake. Failing to report a known incident is a serious
violation.

10 Enforcement
Violations may result in revocation of access, disciplinary action up to and
including termination, and, where applicable, legal action. Suspected criminal
activity is referred to law enforcement.

11 Contacts
Information Security: `security@helios.example.com`
Security Operations Center (24/7): +1-555-0100

doc_title: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
heading_path: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
text:
This policy governs any situation in which a Helios Systems employee performs
  work from a country other than the country of their registered work location,
  regardless of duration and regardless of whether the trip is also a personal
  holiday. It exists because cross-border work creates income-tax, social-
  security, permanent-establishment, immigration, and data-protection exposure
  for both the employee and Helios.

Domestic temporary relocation within the employee's home country is covered by POL-REMOTE-001 Section 5 and is not in scope here.

doc_title: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
heading_path: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
text:
An approved employee may work from an eligible country for a maximum of 30 calendar days per rolling 12-month period , across all
  countries combined. Days are counted as calendar days present in the country
  while performing any work, including partial days.

Requests exceeding 30 days are not approved as temporary international
  remote work . An employee who needs to work abroad for longer than 30
  days must either:

- take the excess period as approved PTO or unpaid leave, performing no work
      whatsoever during that period; or
- pursue a permanent relocation through Global Mobility, which requires an
      entity in the destination country, a new employment agreement, and a
      minimum lead time of 90 days ; or
- be assigned to a formal short-term international assignment, which is
      sponsored by the business unit and requires VP approval.

A six-week (42-day) request, for example, exceeds the 30-day limit and cannot
  be approved as ordinary international remote work.

doc_title: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
heading_path: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
text:
Temporary international remote work is permitted only in countries where
  Helios has assessed the tax and permanent-establishment risk. As of the
  effective date, the eligible list is:

| Country | Max consecutive days | Notes |
| Ireland | 30 | Helios entity present |
| Portugal | 30 | Helios entity present |
| Spain | 21 | No entity; PE risk after 21 days |
| Italy | 21 | No entity; PE risk after 21 days |
| Germany | 21 | No entity; PE risk after 21 days |
| Netherlands | 21 | No entity; PE risk after 21 days |
| United Kingdom | 30 | Treaty relief available |
| Canada | 30 | Ontario and British Columbia only |
| Mexico | 14 | Immigration restrictions |
| Singapore | 30 | Helios entity present |
| Japan | 14 | Immigration restrictions |

Work from any country not on this list is prohibited without a
  case-by-case assessment by Global Mobility & Tax, which requires a minimum
  of 20 business days to complete. Work from countries subject
  to sanctions or export-control restrictions is prohibited outright; see POL-SEC-001 Section 8.

doc_title: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
heading_path: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
text:
1. Employee submits an International Remote Work request in Helios Workday at
      least 20 business days before the intended start date,
      specifying destination country, exact dates, and total calendar days.
2. Manager approval — confirms coverage and time-zone overlap
      under POL-REMOTE-001 Section 8.
3. Global Mobility & Tax review — confirms the country is
      eligible, the day count is within limits, and no permanent-establishment
      or payroll-withholding trigger applies.
4. Immigration check — confirms the employee holds the right
      to be present and, where required, the right to work. Employees on a US
      work visa (including H-1B, L-1, O-1, and TN status) must additionally be
      cleared by Immigration Counsel, as travel may affect status or re-entry.
5. Information Security review — required for all
      international requests, per POL-SEC-001 Section 7.
6. Written approval is issued in Workday. No travel should be booked
      before written approval is issued.

Typical end-to-end approval time is 10 – 20 business days. Requests submitted
  with less than 20 business days' notice are reviewed on a best-effort basis and
  are frequently denied for lack of review time.

doc_title: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
heading_path: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
text:
The employee remains on their home-country payroll for approved periods within
  the limits of Section 2. However:

- Some countries begin taxing employment income from day one of physical
      presence, irrespective of treaty relief. Where this applies, Global
      Mobility will notify the employee during review.
- Helios does not provide tax equalisation, gross-up, or personal tax-return
      preparation for voluntary international remote work. Any additional
      personal tax liability is the employee's responsibility.
- Helios does provide, at company expense, a one-hour consultation with the
      company's external tax adviser for any approved request of 14 days or
      more.
- Exceeding the approved day count can create a permanent establishment for
      Helios in the destination country, with corporate tax consequences. This is
      the single most serious risk addressed by this policy.

doc_title: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
heading_path: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
text:
- Work only on the Helios-issued device; personal devices are prohibited for
      any work purpose while abroad ( POL-SEC-001 Section 3).
- Connect through the Helios VPN for all work activity
      ( POL-SEC-001 Section 7.2).
- Maintain the core collaboration hours agreed with the manager.
- Do not extend the approved dates without submitting a new request. Approval
      is date-specific.
- Do not perform work in a third country not named in the approval, even in
      transit.

doc_title: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
heading_path: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
text:
Voluntary international remote work is not business travel .
  Flights, accommodation, meals, coworking space, and local transport are not reimbursable . See POL-EXP-001 Section 6.4.
  Incremental costs that Helios does require — for example a loaner travel
  laptop, or a mandated eSIM data plan — are reimbursable.

doc_title: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
heading_path: International Remote Work and Tax Compliance Policy
text:
Working from another country without written approval is a policy violation and
  may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination, in addition
  to any personal tax or immigration consequences for the employee. Managers who
  knowingly permit unapproved international work are also accountable under this
  policy.

This policy describes leave available for the birth or placement of a child, for
an employee's own serious health condition, and for the care of a family member
with a serious health condition. Leave under this policy is **separate from PTO**
and is not deducted from the PTO balance (`POL-PTO-001`, Section 1).

| Role in the birth or placement | Paid leave |
| --- | --- |
| Birthing parent | **16 weeks** at 100% of base pay |
| Non-birthing parent, including adoptive and foster | **8 weeks** at 100% of base pay |

Leave applies equally regardless of gender, marital status, or the manner in
which the employee became a parent, including birth, adoption, surrogacy, and
foster placement.

- **12 months of continuous service** at the date leave begins
  (`POL-BEN-001`, Section 4).
- Full-time employees receive the full entitlement. Part-time employees receive
  a pro-rated entitlement based on scheduled hours.
- Temporary employees, interns, and contractors are not eligible.

- Leave must be taken within **12 months** of the birth or placement.
- Leave may be taken in up to **three separate blocks**, each of at least two
  consecutive weeks, with manager agreement on the schedule.
- Birthing parents' leave begins on the date of birth unless a medical
  disability leave begins earlier (Section 3).
- Multiple births or placements do not increase the entitlement.
- Both parents may be Helios employees; each receives their own entitlement.

2.4 Notice
Provide at least **30 days'** notice where the need is foreseeable. Where it is
not foreseeable — for example premature birth or an expedited placement —
notify People Operations as soon as practicable.

Absences of **four (4) or more consecutive days** due to the employee's own
serious health condition are handled under this policy rather than PTO
(`POL-PTO-001`, Section 7). Absences of one to three days are ordinary sick
absences charged to PTO.

Full-time employees are covered by employer-paid short-term disability:

| Period | Benefit |
| --- | --- |
| Days 1 – 7 | Elimination period; employee may use PTO or take unpaid |
| Week 2 – week 8 | 100% of base pay |
| Week 9 – week 26 | 60% of base pay |

Part-time employees are not covered by short-term disability
(`POL-BEN-001`, Section 3) and should contact People Operations to discuss state
disability programs and unpaid leave options.

3.3 Long-Term Disability
Long-term disability begins after 26 weeks of continuous disability and pays 60%
of base pay, subject to the plan document. Full-time employees only.

Medical certification is required for any medical leave of more than five
consecutive business days. Certification is submitted directly to the
third-party leave administrator, **not** to the employee's manager. Managers
receive only the approved leave dates and never the underlying medical
information.

Employees with 12 months of service may take up to **12 weeks** of leave per
rolling 12-month period to care for a spouse, domestic partner, child, or parent
with a serious health condition. The first **4 weeks** are paid at 100% of base
pay; the remainder is unpaid unless the employee elects to apply accrued PTO.

Bereavement leave is available immediately on hire and is not charged to PTO:

| Relationship | Paid days |
| --- | --- |
| Spouse, domestic partner, child, or parent | 10 days |
| Sibling, grandparent, grandchild, parent-in-law | 5 days |
| Other close relationship, including chosen family | 3 days |
| Pregnancy loss or failed adoption or surrogacy | 10 days |

Additional unpaid time may be approved by the manager. Travel-related time is
included within the days above.

- **Job protection:** Leave under this policy runs concurrently with FMLA and
  with any applicable state leave program where the law permits.
- **Holidays:** Company holidays falling within a leave period are covered by
  the leave benefit and are not separately credited
  (`POL-HOL-001`, Section 6).
- **PTO accrual:** PTO continues to accrue during paid leave. PTO does not
  accrue during unpaid leave beyond 30 days.
- **Benefits:** Medical, dental, and vision coverage continues unchanged during
  approved leave. The employee remains responsible for their premium share.
- **401(k):** Deferrals pause during unpaid leave; the company match resumes on
  return.

- Employees return to the same position, or an equivalent position with
  equivalent pay, benefits, and responsibilities.
- Return-to-work dates may be adjusted once, by up to two weeks, with 10
  business days' notice to the manager.
- Birthing parents are entitled to a **phased return**: four weeks at 80%
  schedule and 100% pay, on request.
- Lactation space and reasonable break time are provided at every Helios office
  and must be accommodated for remote employees' schedules.

1. Notify People Operations at `leave@helios.example.com`, ideally 30 days in
   advance.
2. People Operations opens a case with the third-party leave administrator.
3. The administrator contacts the employee directly for any certification.
4. The employee's manager receives only the approved dates.
5. A written leave confirmation is issued before the leave begins.

Employees should not disclose medical details to their manager and managers must
not request them. Doing so is a privacy violation under `POL-CONDUCT-001`.

This policy describes how performance is set, reviewed, and rated at Helios
Systems, and how promotion and compensation decisions are made.

Helios runs **two review cycles per year**:

| Cycle | Period covered | Review window | Outcomes effective |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H1 | January – June | July 1 – July 31 | August 1 |
| H2 | July – December | January 5 – January 31 | February 1 |

Employees who joined fewer than **90 days** before the start of a review window
receive a written check-in instead of a formal rating and are not eligible for a
merit increase in that cycle.

| Rating | Meaning | Approx. distribution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Exceptional** | Consistently exceeded role expectations with outsized impact | ~10% |
| **Exceeds Expectations** | Delivered above role expectations | ~25% |
| **Meets Expectations** | Delivered the role well and reliably | ~55% |
| **Partially Meets** | Fell short in one or more significant areas | ~8% |
| **Does Not Meet** | Substantially failed to deliver role expectations | ~2% |

Distributions are guidance for calibration, not quotas. A manager is never
required to assign a low rating to fit a distribution.

**"Meets Expectations" is a good rating.** It is the expected outcome for a
strong performer delivering their role, and it satisfies the performance
requirement for fully remote eligibility under `POL-REMOTE-001` §3.

- Employee self-assessment.
- Manager assessment against the role's level expectations in the job
  architecture.
- Peer feedback from at least two colleagues, selected jointly by the employee
  and manager.
- Goal outcomes agreed at the start of the cycle.

Reviews assess **what** was delivered and **how** it was delivered. Conduct
inconsistent with `POL-CONDUCT-001` caps the rating at "Partially Meets"
regardless of delivery.

Ratings are calibrated in a group session at the department level before being
shared with employees, to reduce inconsistency between managers. Calibration
notes are confidential. An employee may ask their manager for the rationale
behind their rating at any time.

| Rating | Typical merit increase | Equity refresh | Bonus multiplier |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Exceptional | 6 – 10% | Yes, above target | 1.3 – 1.5x |
| Exceeds Expectations | 4 – 6% | Yes, at target | 1.1 – 1.3x |
| Meets Expectations | 2 – 4% | Yes, at target | 1.0x |
| Partially Meets | 0 – 2% | No | 0.5x |
| Does Not Meet | 0% | No | 0x |

Merit increases are effective on the cycle dates in Section 2. Compensation is
also reviewed against market benchmarks annually; a market adjustment may be
made outside the merit process.

Promotion recognises sustained performance **at the next level**, not
exceptional performance at the current level. The criteria are:

1. Demonstrated operation at the next level's scope for at least **two
   consecutive review cycles**.
2. A rating of "Exceeds Expectations" or higher in the most recent cycle.
3. A written promotion case prepared by the manager, evidencing next-level
   scope, impact, and behaviours.
4. Endorsement in the department calibration session.
5. Approval by the skip-level manager and the HR Business Partner.

7.2 Timing
Promotions are decided within the two review cycles. Off-cycle promotions are
permitted only where a role has materially changed, and require VP approval.

7.3 Time in Role
There is no minimum time in role, but the two-cycle evidence requirement in
Section 7.1 means promotion typically occurs after at least 12 months at a
level.

A PIP is used where performance is rated "Partially Meets" or "Does Not Meet",
or where a significant performance concern arises between cycles. A PIP must be
preceded by documented, specific feedback and a reasonable opportunity to
improve.
citation: POL-PERF-001 §8.1 When a PIP Is Used

text:
- Duration: **60 days**, extendable once by 30 days.
- Contains specific, measurable objectives and a weekly check-in cadence.
- Reviewed and approved by the HR Business Partner before it is issued.
- The employee may request a support person at PIP meetings.

While on an active PIP an employee is **not eligible** for:

- promotion;
- a merit increase or equity refresh;
- an internal transfer; or
- a change to fully remote work arrangement (`POL-REMOTE-001` §3.3).

Successful completion of a PIP restores eligibility immediately. A PIP is not a
prelude to a predetermined outcome; the majority of Helios PIPs conclude
successfully.

Employees may apply for an internal role after **12 months** in their current
role, provided they are not on an active PIP and their most recent rating is
"Meets Expectations" or higher. The current manager is notified when the
employee reaches the interview stage, not at application.

An employee who disagrees with a rating may:

1. discuss it with their manager and add a written employee comment to the
   review record, which is retained permanently;
2. raise it with their HR Business Partner; and
3. request a review by the skip-level manager within **14 days** of receiving
   the rating.

Raising a concern about a review is protected activity; retaliation for doing so
violates `POL-CONDUCT-001` §3.5.

Helios Systems, Inc. ("Helios") provides paid time off so that employees can
rest, attend to personal matters, and return to work refreshed. This policy
describes how PTO is accrued, requested, approved, and paid out.

This policy applies to all US-based employees. Contractors and interns are not
eligible for PTO; see `POL-BEN-001` (Benefits and Eligibility) for the
definitions of employment type. Statutory leave — including parental leave and
serious-health-condition leave — is governed separately by `POL-LEAVE-002`
(Parental and Medical Leave) and is **not** deducted from the PTO balance.

PTO accrues on a per-pay-period basis (24 pay periods per year). Accrual rate is
determined by employment type and completed years of service:

| Employment type | Years of service | Annual accrual | Per pay period |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Full-time (>= 30 hrs/week) | 0 – 2 years | 15 days (120 hrs) | 5.00 hrs |
| Full-time | 3 – 5 years | 20 days (160 hrs) | 6.67 hrs |
| Full-time | 6+ years | 25 days (200 hrs) | 8.33 hrs |
| Part-time (20 – 29 hrs/week) | Any | Pro-rated at 0.5x full-time | 2.50 hrs |
| Temporary / Intern | Any | Not eligible | — |

Years of service are measured from the employee's `hire_date`. An employee whose
service anniversary falls mid-year moves to the higher accrual rate on the first
pay period following the anniversary.

PTO accrual stops once an employee's balance reaches **1.5x their annual accrual
rate**. Accrual resumes automatically once the balance falls below the cap.
Helios does not retroactively grant PTO that was not accrued because of the cap.

Employees may carry over a maximum of **10 days (80 hours)** into the next
calendar year. Balances above 10 days as of December 31 are forfeited, except
where state law requires otherwise (see Section 8).

Advance notice requirements scale with the length of the absence:

| Length of absence | Minimum advance notice |
| --- | --- |
| 1 – 2 consecutive business days | 3 business days |
| 3 – 5 consecutive business days | 10 business days |
| 6 – 10 consecutive business days | 20 business days |
| More than 10 consecutive business days | 30 business days, plus skip-level approval |

Requests submitted with less than the minimum notice are not automatically
denied, but require documented manager approval and a stated business
justification.

1. The employee submits a PTO request in Helios Workday, specifying start date,
   end date, and total hours.
2. The request routes to the employee's direct manager of record.
3. The manager approves or denies within **3 business days**. If a manager does
   not respond within 3 business days, the request escalates automatically to
   the skip-level manager.
4. Approved requests are deducted from the PTO balance on the first day of the
   absence, not at the time of approval.

Employees must not book non-refundable travel before receiving written approval.

An employee may not take PTO they have not accrued. If a requested absence
exceeds the available balance, the employee may:

- reduce the length of the absence to fit the available balance;
- request unpaid personal leave, which requires skip-level approval; or
- apply an unused floating holiday (see `POL-HOL-001`, Section 3).

Negative PTO balances are not permitted under any circumstances.

To protect delivery and customer commitments, the following are blackout
periods during which PTO requests of **3 or more consecutive days** are
generally denied:

- **Fiscal close:** the last 5 business days and first 3 business days of each
  fiscal quarter (fiscal quarters end March 31, June 30, September 30,
  December 31).
- **Annual customer conference:** the week of the Helios Forum conference
  (September 14 – 18, 2026).
- **Peak support season (Customer Support org only):** November 15 – January 5.

Exceptions to a blackout period require VP-level approval. Blackout periods do
not apply to statutory leave under `POL-LEAVE-002`, to bereavement leave, or to
jury duty.

No more than **25% of a team** may be on PTO simultaneously. Where 25% of the
team is fewer than one person, at least one person may still take PTO. Managers
resolve competing requests for the same dates in the order the requests were
submitted.

6 Holidays Falling Within PTO
Company-observed holidays that fall within an approved PTO absence are **not**
deducted from the PTO balance. See `POL-HOL-001` for the observed holiday
schedule.

Helios operates a combined PTO bank; there is no separate sick-time balance for
absences of 1 – 3 days. Absences of **4 or more consecutive days** due to the
employee's own serious health condition are handled under `POL-LEAVE-002`
(Parental and Medical Leave) and are not charged to PTO.

Employees should notify their manager as early as possible on the first day of
an unplanned sick absence. No advance notice is required for sick absences.

Accrued, unused PTO is paid out at separation at the employee's base rate of pay
in states where payout is legally required, including California, Colorado, and
Illinois. In all other states, Helios pays out accrued, unused PTO up to a
maximum of **10 days (80 hours)**.

Employees must submit final PTO requests before their last day of employment.
PTO may not be used to extend a separation date.

PTO is intended for genuine disconnection. Employees on PTO are not expected to
monitor email or respond to messages. Managers must not require work during
approved PTO. An employee who is recalled to work during approved PTO has the
corresponding hours credited back to their balance.

Working remotely from another location is **not** PTO and must instead follow
`POL-REMOTE-001` (Remote and Hybrid Work Policy).

10 Policy Questions and Exceptions
Questions about this policy should be directed to People Operations at
`people-ops@helios.example.com`. Exceptions must be approved in writing by the
VP of People Operations and are documented in the employee's record.

Helios Systems supports flexible work arrangements where they are compatible
with the employee's role, team needs, and legal obligations. This policy defines
the available work arrangements, who is eligible for each, and how to request a
change.

Temporary work from a location outside the employee's home country is governed
by `POL-INTL-001` (International Remote Work and Tax Compliance) and requires
additional approvals.

2 Work Arrangement Types
Every employee is assigned exactly one of three work arrangements, recorded as
`work_arrangement` in the HR system.

2.1 Onsite
The employee works from an assigned Helios office five days per week. Onsite is
required for roles with physical-presence requirements, including hardware lab
engineering, facilities, and IT asset management.

The employee works from an assigned Helios office a minimum of **three (3) days
per week**, with anchor days set by their team. The remaining days may be worked
from an approved remote location within commuting distance.

Hybrid is the default arrangement for employees assigned to an office location.

The employee has no assigned office and works from a registered home address.
Remote employees are expected to travel to a Helios office for team onsites up
to **four (4) times per year** at company expense, governed by `POL-EXP-001`.

An employee is eligible to request fully remote status only if **all** of the
following are true:

1. The employee has completed at least **six (6) months** of continuous service
   at Helios.
2. The employee's most recent performance rating is **"Meets Expectations" or
   higher** (see `POL-PERF-001`).
3. The employee is not currently on a performance improvement plan.
4. The role is designated remote-eligible in the job architecture. Roles
   designated `Onsite Required` are not eligible under any circumstances.
5. The employee's registered work location is a US state, or a country, in which
   Helios is a registered employer. As of the effective date these are:
   **United States** (all states except Alaska and Hawaii), **Ireland**,
   **Singapore**, **Canada** (Ontario and British Columbia only), and
   **Portugal**.

Employees in their first six months may still work hybrid; the six-month
requirement applies only to fully remote status.
citation: POL-REMOTE-001 §3 Eligibility for Fully Remote Status

text:
1. The employee submits a Work Arrangement Change request in Helios Workday.
2. The direct manager reviews for team-coverage impact and approves or denies.
3. For a change **to fully remote**, the skip-level manager and the HR Business
   Partner must also approve.
4. Approved changes take effect at the start of the next full pay period.
5. Approved changes to the registered work address trigger a payroll and tax
   review, which may take up to **15 business days**.

An employee may request a change no more than twice per calendar year.
citation: POL-REMOTE-001 §4 Requesting or Changing an Arrangement

text:
An employee may work temporarily from a US location other than their registered
address without changing their work arrangement, subject to duration limits:

| Duration | Approval required | Additional requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 – 10 consecutive business days | Manager notification only | None |
| 11 – 20 consecutive business days | Manager written approval | Security review under `POL-SEC-001` §7 |
| 21 – 30 consecutive business days | Manager + HR Business Partner | Security review + payroll notification |
| More than 30 consecutive days in a state where the employee is not registered | Not permitted as temporary work | Requires a permanent work-location change under Section 4 |

The **30-day rule** exists because working more than 30 days in a state creates
state income-tax withholding and, in some states, employer-registration
obligations. Cumulative days in the same state within a rolling 12-month period
count toward the 30-day threshold.

heading_path: 6. Temporary Work Outside the Home Country
section: Temporary Work Outside the Home Country
text:
Working from outside the employee's home country — for any duration — is **not**
covered by Section 5. It requires prior approval under `POL-INTL-001`, which
imposes a separate day limit, tax review, immigration check, and security
review. Booking travel before receiving approval under `POL-INTL-001` is at the
employee's own risk.
citation: POL-REMOTE-001 §6 Temporary Work Outside the Home Country

text:
Employees working remotely must maintain a workspace that:

- has a reliable internet connection of at least **25 Mbps download / 5 Mbps
  upload**;
- is private enough to hold confidential conversations without being overheard,
  as required by `POL-SEC-001` §4;
- is free of recognised safety hazards; and
- is located at the address registered in the HR system.

Helios provides a one-time home-office stipend and ongoing equipment support
under `POL-EQUIP-001`.

All employees, regardless of arrangement, must be available during core
collaboration hours of **10:00 – 15:00 in their registered location's local
time zone**, Monday through Friday.

Employees temporarily working from a time zone more than **6 hours** offset from
their team's primary time zone must agree an overlap schedule with their manager
in advance. This applies to both domestic and international temporary work.

Remote and hybrid work are conditional privileges, not entitlements. Helios may
modify or revoke an individual's arrangement where there is a documented
performance concern, a change in role requirements, or non-compliance with this
policy.

Working from an unregistered location, or exceeding the limits in Section 5 or
`POL-INTL-001` without approval, may expose both the employee and Helios to tax
and immigration liability and is treated as a policy violation under
`POL-CONDUCT-001`.

Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy
citation: POL-EXP-001 — Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy

text:
Helios Systems reimburses reasonable, necessary, and documented expenses
incurred in the course of business. Employees should spend Helios money as
carefully as their own, choose the lower-cost reasonable option, and submit
accurate claims promptly.

2.1 Deadlines
Expenses must be submitted within 60 calendar days of being incurred.
Claims submitted after 60 days require Director approval, and claims submitted
after 120 days cannot be reimbursed under any circumstances.

An itemised receipt is required for every expense of $25 or more. A credit
card statement line is not an itemised receipt. Expenses under $25 may be
claimed without a receipt, up to $150 per expense report.
Receipts must show the vendor, date, itemised amounts, and total. For meals with
other people, the claim must also list the attendees and the business purpose.

Total expense report a  Approver
Up to $500              Direct manager
$501 - $2,500           Direct manager + Direc
$2,501 - $10,000        Director + VP
Over $10,000            VP + Finance Business
Pre-approval is required for any single expense over $2,500 and for all
international business travel.

- Book through the Helios travel portal (Navan). Bookings outside the portal
  require documented justification and are reimbursed at the lower of actual
  cost or the portal fare for the same itinerary.
- Economy class is required for all flights with a scheduled duration under
  6 hours.
- Premium economy is permitted for flights of 6 hours or more.
- Business class requires VP approval and is permitted only for flights of
  10 hours or more.
- Book at least 14 days in advance where the itinerary is known.
- Seat selection up to $75 per segment and one checked bag are reimbursable.
- Travel upgrades purchased with personal funds or points are not reimbursable.

- Reimbursable up to $300 per night in Tier 1 cities (New York, San
  Francisco, London, Tokyo, Singapore, Zurich) and $200 per night elsewhere,
  excluding taxes and mandatory fees.
- Short-term rentals are permitted at or below the applicable nightly cap.
- Room-service and minibar charges are reimbursable only within the meal per
  diem in Section 5.
- In-room movies, spa services, and laundry for trips under 5 nights are not
  reimbursable.

Meals on business travel are reimbursed on a per diem basis, not by actual
receipt, except for business meals with customers or candidates.
Location tier           Daily per diem
Tier 1 cities           $85
United States, other    $65
International, other    $70
Partial travel days are reimbursed at 75% of the per diem. Meals provided by the
company or included in a conference fee reduce the per diem for that day by:
breakfast $15, lunch $25, dinner $40.
Business meals with customers, partners, or candidates are reimbursed at actual
cost with an itemised receipt and a documented attendee list. Alcohol is
reimbursable only at customer or candidate meals and must be itemised
separately; alcohol is never reimbursable on a per-diem day.

Travel, accommodation, meals, coworking space, and local transport associated
with voluntary international remote work under POL-INTL-001 are not
business travel and are not reimbursable. Only costs Helios specifically
mandates -- for example an Information Security-required loaner device or a
required eSIM data plan -- are reimbursable, and must be pre-approved.

- Rideshare and taxi are reimbursable for business travel and for late-night
  travel from the office after 21:00.
- Rental cars are reimbursable at mid-size class or below; premium classes
  require Director approval. Decline the rental company's collision waiver in
  the United States, where Helios corporate insurance applies; accept it
  internationally.
- Personal vehicle mileage is reimbursed at the current IRS standard rate,
  measured from the office or from home, whichever is shorter.
- Airport parking is reimbursable for trips of up to 7 days; for longer trips,
  claim the lower of parking or round-trip rideshare.

Employees must not purchase computing equipment, peripherals, or software
directly and claim reimbursement. All such purchases are made by IT under
POL-EQUIP-001. Direct purchases will be denied.
Ergonomic furniture and accessories are handled through the home-office stipend
in POL-BEN-001 Section 8, not as an expense claim.

Employees who travel more than four times per year are issued a Helios corporate
card. Corporate card transactions must still be reconciled in an expense report
within 60 days. Personal use of the corporate card is prohibited; incidental
personal charges must be repaid within 30 days.

Finance audits a random 10% of expense reports each month, plus all reports over
$5,000. Knowingly submitting a false or inflated claim is treated as a serious
violation under POL-CONDUCT-001 and may result in termination and recovery of
funds.
